s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation identified on genetic analysis
key_facts: patient is a man in his 40s
patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
patient has undergone radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
lesion developed in early January 2015
lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
lesion is 4 cm in diameter
histopathological analysis shows normal epidermis
genetic analysis was performed using paired whole-exome sequencing of affected tissue and patient's blood

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive vascular tumor with potential for metastasis, consistent with patient's history of cancer

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: vascular tumor associated with immunosuppression, possible in patient with history of chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: rare condition involving angiosarcoma in lymphedematous limbs, plausible given patient's cancer history

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma with KDR mutation
shortlist.why_kept: rare vascular tumor with KDR mutation, matching patient's genetic analysis findings

shortlist.label: Atypical vascular lesion
shortlist.why_kept: lesion's unusual presentation and patient's cancer history suggest possibility of atypical vascular lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque with telangiectasias and the identification of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation in the affected tissue are consistent with an atypical vascular lesion, particularly in the context of the patient's history of cancer treatment.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more aggressive features and is less likely to be a single, well-defined lesion

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually associated with human herpesvirus 8 infection and has distinct histological features not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Refers to angiosarcoma arising in the context of chronic lymphedema, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma with KDR mutation
rejected.why: While the KDR mutation is consistent with this diagnosis, the clinical and histological features described do not fully align with retiform hemangioendothelioma

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Does not match the histopathological analysis and genetic findings presented
